selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-worker created as a managed (systemd) service and running as a long-running background worker
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; systemctl status shows Active: active (running) with the worker process and its sleep child under the service cgroup; state.json tick counter increments across polls, proving continuous long-running operation.

selected_evidence.requirement: Service confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory
selected_evidence.summary: Directory listing shows state.json/worker.log owned by inventory-worker only inside /var/lib/inventory. An ephemeral probe run as the same user with the same sandbox properties (ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory) succeeded writing inside /var/lib/inventory but failed with 'Read-only file system' when attempting to write to /tmp and /etc, empirically falsifying/confirming the write confinement.
systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes for the unit; /proc/<MainPID>/status of the actually running process confirms NoNewPrivs:	1 at the kernel level.
Captured boot_id 98aa35f5-6905-42fd-9f07-0e28f75b4fa6, uptime -s, systemctl is-active/is-enabled=active/enabled, and live state.json tick=5 as pre-restart baseline.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 1; systemctl reboot' via nohup+disown; the exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' successfully before the node dropped, and the next call failed with connection reset, confirming the reboot took effect.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Node was unreachable (connection reset, then timeouts) during reboot, then became reachable again with boot_id 187948fa-e868-408c-9a20-dfce798bb9a3, different from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual kernel restart occurred (not just a service bounce).

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 service and data recovered after restart, quorum/health confirmed (single-node, no cluster)
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot uptime -s reset to the new boot time; inventory-worker.service is active/enabled again with a new MainPID; state.json and worker.log persisted in /var/lib/inventory and the tick counter resumed incrementing (tick 5 -> 7), proving both service and data recovery.

commands.command:
cat > /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
DATA_DIR=/var/lib/inventory
STATE_FILE="$DATA_DIR/state.json"
LOG_FILE="$DATA_DIR/worker.log"

i=0
while :; do
  i=$((i + 1))
  ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  printf '{"tick":%s,"timestamp":"%s"}\n' "$i" "$ts" > "$STATE_FILE.tmp"
  mv "$STATE_FILE.tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
  echo "$ts tick=$i" >> "$LOG_FILE"
  sleep 5
done
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh
cat /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh

commands.command:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Inventory background worker
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=inventory-worker
Group=inventory-worker
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2

NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory
ReadOnlyPaths=/usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh
StateDirectory=inventory
StateDirectoryMode=0750
PrivateDevices=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectKernelLogs=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
ProtectClock=true
ProtectHostname=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
RestrictRealtime=true
RestrictNamespaces=true
LockPersonality=true
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true
RemoveIPC=true
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=
SystemCallFilter=@system-service
SystemCallErrorNumber=EPERM
UMask=0027

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

sleep 2
